public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 376

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/376](https://www.erdosproblems.com/376)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos376

/--
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that ${2n\choose n}$ is coprime to $105$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_376 : answer(sorry) ↔ { (n : ℕ) | n.centralBinom.Coprime 105 }.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75] have shown that, for any two odd primes $p$ and $q$,
there are infinite many $n$ such that ${2n\choose n}$ is coprime to $pq$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_376.variants.prime {p q : ℕ} (h₁ : p.Prime)
    (h₂ : Odd p) (h₃ : q.Prime) (h₄ : Odd q) :
    { (n : ℕ) | n.centralBinom.Coprime (p * q) }.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos376

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement quantifies over all odd primes p, q, including p = q. The source ('for any two odd primes p and q') could be read as meaning distinct primes.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If the Lean version holds, the distinct-primes version holds by specialisation. Conversely, suppose the distinct-primes version holds, and take p = q. Pick an odd prime r ≠ p (3 or 5). Every n with C(2n,n) coprime to p·r has C(2n,n) coprime to p, because p ∣ p·r, and hence coprime to p·p. So {n | coprime to p·p} contains an infinite set and is infinite. The two statements are therefore equivalent.

review.notes:
Both declarations match erdosproblems.com/376.

(1) erdos_376: `answer(sorry) ↔ {n : ℕ | n.centralBinom.Coprime 105}.Infinite` is the source's question with the right polarity. `Nat.centralBinom n = (2n).choose n` and `Nat.Coprime` means gcd = 1 (checked with #print). n = 0 is in the set (centralBinom 0 = 1), which cannot change whether the set is infinite. By #eval, the Lean set's members below 3300 are 0, 1, 10, 756, 757, 3160, 3186, 3187, 3250. This matches the initial terms of A030979 as quoted in secondary sources, and Pomerance's 'n = 1, 10, and 756'. The set also agrees for all n < 4000 with the source's Kummer digit rule: base-3 digits ≤ 1, base-5 digits ≤ 2, base-7 digits ≤ 3. Tagged `research open`; the source page still says OPEN, and problems.yaml says open. No status issue.

(2) erdos_376.variants.prime: the hypotheses (p, q prime and odd) are exactly the source's 'two odd primes'. The EGRS75 abstract says only 'for any two primes p and q'. It must mean odd primes: C(2n,n) is even for every n ≥ 1, and #eval confirms only n = 0 is coprime to 2·3. The paper derives the result from its Theorem 1 with A = (p−1)/2, which needs p odd. Pomerance and erdosproblems.com both state it for odd primes. `research solved` is correct. The hypotheses are satisfiable (e.g. 3 and 5). The p = q case is harmless; the equivalence is proved in Lean (see reformulations).

Only a cosmetic slip, not a mathematical defect: the variant's docstring says 'infinite many' instead of 'infinitely many'.

Access notes: erdosproblems.com, oeis.org and ams.org were all behind Cloudflare challenges. I read the erdosproblems page through a reader proxy. OEIS A030979 itself was not fetched; its initial terms were recomputed in Lean instead. The OEIS page is not needed to judge the file.
